_comment: AASB S2 — Australian Sustainability Reporting Standards. Phased by size in
three groups, each caught by meeting at least two of three size tests, or by
an NGER or asset-owner trigger regardless of size.
aasb.gov.au could not be reached from the build environment, so thresholds
and dates come from professional-firm and practitioner summaries and are
graded medium. Verify before a scoping decision rests on them.
markets.name: Australia
markets.standard: AASB S2 Climate-related Disclosures (Australian Sustainability Reporting Standards)

markets.test: At least two of the three size tests, on a consolidated basis. An NGER publication-threshold reporter or a qualifying asset owner is caught regardless of size.

cohorts.name: Group 1
cohorts.note: The largest entities. First annual reporting periods began on or after 1 January 2025, with the first reports lodged for December 2025 year ends.

cohorts.name: Group 2
cohorts.also: NGER reporters not in Group 1, and asset owners with AUD 5bn or more under management
cohorts.note: Entered their first mandatory reporting period on 1 July 2026.

cohorts.name: Group 3
cohorts.note: Financial years beginning on or after 1 July 2027.

markets.scope3: Not required in an entity's first AASB S2 reporting period; mandatory from the second.
markets.assurance: Phased to reasonable assurance over the full disclosure by 2030.
markets.reliefs: A three-year modified liability regime limits private litigation over certain forward-looking climate statements in the early years.

_comment: The ISSB baseline itself, as a market row rather than a jurisdiction. IFRS S1
and S2 bind nobody on their own — a jurisdiction has to adopt them — which is
the single most misunderstood thing about the standard and the reason this
file exists rather than being folded into the others.
Adoption count is deliberately expressed as a floor, not a precise number:
jurisdictions move between 'adopted', 'aligned' and 'consulting' and no
reachable source gives a stable figure.
markets.name: ISSB

sources.title: Use of IFRS Standards by jurisdiction

markets.test: Nothing on its own. IFRS S2 applies where a jurisdiction has adopted or aligned to it — Australia and Singapore below are two such jurisdictions.

cohorts.name: Adopting jurisdictions
cohorts.also: Set by each jurisdiction, not by the ISSB
cohorts.note: More than 30 jurisdictions have adopted or aligned. The commencement date, the entities caught and the assurance requirement are all local decisions.

markets.scope3: Required under paragraph 29(a), with a one-year transition relief allowing first-time reporters to omit it in year one.
markets.assurance: Set by the adopting jurisdiction; the standard itself does not require it.
markets.reliefs: First-year reliefs cover Scope 3, comparatives, and reporting timing relative to the financial statements.
markets.digital_tagging: An IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Taxonomy exists; mandating its use is a jurisdictional decision.

_comment: Singapore — ISSB-aligned climate reporting, run jointly by SGX RegCo for
listed issuers and ACRA for large non-listed companies.
The timeline moved in August 2025: ACRA and SGX RegCo extended it, and the
large non-listed company obligation was pushed from FY2027 to FY2030. Any
tool still quoting FY2027 for non-listed companies is out of date.
acra.gov.sg could not be reached from the build environment, so this comes
from law-firm and practitioner summaries and is graded medium.
markets.name: Singapore
markets.standard: IFRS S2 as adopted for Singapore reporting

sources.title: Sustainability reporting and assurance requirements — timeline

markets.test: Listing status first: every SGX-listed issuer is caught. A large non-listed company is caught on both revenue and assets, not either.

cohorts.name: SGX-listed issuers
cohorts.also: All listed issuers, regardless of size
cohorts.note: Climate disclosures aligned with IFRS S2 from FY2025, with Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions from the same year.

cohorts.name: STI constituents — Scope 3
cohorts.note: Scope 3 becomes mandatory for STI constituents from FY2026. For other listed issuers it stays voluntary.

cohorts.name: Large non-listed companies
cohorts.note: Revenue of at least SGD 1bn AND total assets of at least SGD 500mn. Deferred from FY2027 to FY2030 by ACRA's August 2025 update.

markets.scope3: Mandatory for STI constituents from FY2026; voluntary for other listed issuers.
markets.assurance: External limited assurance over Scope 1 and 2, phased with the reporting timeline.
markets.reliefs: The August 2025 update extended the timeline generally, explicitly to let companies build reporting capacity.
